---
title: "Krigging & IDW example - Meuse river sediments"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(sp)
library(sf)
library(gstat)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales) # for "comma"
library(magrittr)
data(meuse)
data(meuse.grid)
```

* We shall be predicting zinc-sediment levels.  

* Example is based on the Meuse dataset.  

```{r}
glimpse(meuse)
glimpse(meuse.grid) # empty grid - zinc levels will be predicted here
```

* We can use `ggplot2` to visually inspect how zinc varies over the domain of interest where we map concentration to point size:

```{r}
meuse %>% 
  as.data.frame %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) + geom_point(aes(size=zinc), color="red", alpha=3/4) + 
    ggtitle("Zinc Concentration (ppm)") + coord_equal() + theme_bw()
```


----

* Prepare data for spatial analysis (IDW, krigging) by making the DF *spatially aware*:


```{r, warning=F}
meuse <- meuse %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"),crs = 28992,remove=FALSE) # keep the x,y columns

meuse.grid <- meuse.grid %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"),crs = 28992,remove=FALSE)
```

----

## IDW

```{r, warning=F}
idwmodel <- idw(log(zinc) ~1, meuse,meuse.grid,
               maxdist = Inf, idp = 1) 
head(idwmodel) # show interpolated values (note absence of variances of interpolated values)
idwmodel %>% 
  mutate(
    x = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    y = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>% 
  as.data.frame %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=var1.pred)) + coord_equal() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "yellow2", high="red") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels=comma) + scale_y_continuous(labels=comma) +
    theme_bw()
```

* IDV with high `idp` argument produces "tiles" (Voronoi-type)

```{r, warning=F}
idwmodel2 <- idw(log(zinc) ~1, meuse,meuse.grid,
               maxdist = Inf, idp = 20) 
idwmodel2 %>% 
  mutate(
    x = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    y = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>% 
  as.data.frame %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=var1.pred)) + coord_equal() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "yellow2", high="red") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels=comma) + scale_y_continuous(labels=comma) +
    theme_bw()
```

----

## Krigging (ordinary krigging)


1. Calculate the sample variogram. This is done with the `variogram()` function.  

2. Fit a model to the sample variogram using `fit.variogram()` function  

3. Use the fitted variogram for krigging ($\lambda_i$) weights, using `krige()` function  

4. Plot the krigged data using `ggplot()`  


```{r, warning=F, message=F}
# 1
SV <- variogram(log(zinc)~1, meuse) # calculates sample variogram values 
# 2 
lzn.fit <- fit.variogram(SV, vgm("Sph"))
# 3
lzn.kriged <- krige(log(zinc) ~ 1, meuse, meuse.grid, model=lzn.fit)
head(lzn.kriged) # show krigged values and the variances of predictions
# 4
lzn.kriged %>% 
  mutate(
    x = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    y = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>% 
  as.data.frame %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=var1.pred)) + coord_equal() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "yellow2", high="red") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels=comma) + scale_y_continuous(labels=comma) +
    theme_bw()

# show variance of the fitted (krigged) values
lzn.kriged %>% 
  mutate(
    x = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    y = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>% 
  as.data.frame %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=var1.var)) + coord_equal() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high="red") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels=comma) + scale_y_continuous(labels=comma) +
    theme_bw()
```


## Universal krigging

- Universal kriging, more specifically kriging with an external drift, is used next because `dist` is included as a predictor of the spatial trend.  
- The variogram and kriging formulas should describe the same mean structure.  
- Conceptually, the model now is:

$$\log(\textit{zinc}(\pmb{s})) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \textit{dist}(\pmb{s}) + \varepsilon(\pmb{s}),$$

where `dist` explains the deterministic trend and the spatially correlated residual $\varepsilon(\pmb{s})$ is handled through the semivariogram.

```{r, warning=F, message=F}
# 1
SV2 <- variogram(log(zinc)~dist, meuse) # calculates sample variogram values 
# 2 
lzn.fit2 <- fit.variogram(SV2, vgm("Sph"))
# 3
lzn.kriged2 <- krige(log(zinc) ~ dist, meuse, meuse.grid, model=lzn.fit2)
head(lzn.kriged2) # show krigged values and the variances of predictions
# 4
lzn.kriged2 %>% 
  mutate(
    x = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    y = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>% 
  as.data.frame %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=var1.pred)) + coord_equal() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "yellow2", high="red") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels=comma) + scale_y_continuous(labels=comma) +
    theme_bw()

# show variance of the fitted (krigged) values
lzn.kriged2 %>% 
  mutate(
    x = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    y = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>% 
  as.data.frame %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=var1.var)) + coord_equal() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high="red") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels=comma) + scale_y_continuous(labels=comma) +
    theme_bw()


# compare estimated variance for the two krigging-based predictions:

# Ordinary krigging
summary(lzn.kriged$var1.var)

# Universal krigging
summary(lzn.kriged2$var1.var)

```
